title: The War in Words William and Lydia
text: You're watching the History Channel. Coming up at 8, Hell on Wheels, Hitler's secret supercar. But now, it's the war in words. Letters from the Front. The letters of English fighter pilot William McIntosh of the Royal Air Force to his wife, Lydia. My dearest Lydia, ever since we crossed the Channel to France, I have seen nothing but death and destruction. Yet in this darkness, you provide light. Though I may be in hell, you are my perfect angel. Your husband, William. Dear William, thank you. Love, Lydia. Dear wife, you're welcome. In future letters, though, if ever at a loss for words, please find some. For your words remind me of the home I miss so dearly. How I long to see you and our son. I even miss that rambunctious dog of ours. Yours, William. Dear William, I miss our dog, too. Love, Lydia. My dear Lydia, why do you miss our dog? Is he not with you at home? Please send word that he's okay. And also, send some token of your affection so that I may be reminded of you and our son always. Yours, William. Dear William, I am enclosing a lock of my hair. Hold it close and be safe. Love, Lydia. Lydia, dearest, perhaps you have been too generous with your gift of hair. You have sent me a vast amount. You've shorn your head completely bald. Concerned. William, love, Lydia. Give our dog a rub on the belly for me. Run off. As if today could not get worse, my dear friend Christopher was killed on patrol. A young French woman who cared for him in his final moments told me he died honorably. Shame. Love, William. William, so who's this French bitch you're chanting? Your wife, Lydia. Lydia, my dear, there's no cause for jealousy. I only have eyes for you, love. My absence is clearly weighing on you. Perhaps a weekend away would raise your spirits. Devotedly, William. William, I took your advice and went on a little trip. And would you believe there was a newsreel camera at my hotel? I'm sending a copy of the film. Enjoy the show. Your movie star wife... Lydia. My God, Lydia. I cannot believe what I've just seen. You appear to be palling around with Adolf Hitler and his friends as if you were one of the gang. What led to this? I demand an explanation. Your horrified husband, William. Dear William. Oh, I see. So when you talk to some French whore, it's, it was nothing, move on. But when I go to a party where there happens to be a man, it's, I demand an explanation. Yes, because it's Hitler! I am only glad your father is not alive to see what a hypocrite you've become. Love, Lydia. Darling Lydia, has my father passed away? It's the first I'm hearing of this. How did he go? Also still rabidly curious about the Hitler of it all. Answers, please. William. William. I think your father died of a broken heart. He just couldn't live. He couldn't bear to go on without your mother. Love, Lydia. My mother passed as well! Darling, I do not think we should write to each other anymore. But know that I love you and our son dearly. Give him a kiss for me and tell him to be a brave lad. Love, William. William. Tell him yourself. Love, Lydia. Why would you send a five-year-old to a war zone? I would rather not see him again. Will you let him go? Yes, I will. Oh, by the way, this is my first time seeing you here. You should do me another sorrow, and you don't deserve to be in my life. Or your brother can. I am going to see you, to see your father. I will be with you, and I will see your brother, and I will see your brother. I am going to see your father. We'll meet again.
